answer: Make identity pay in memory, not just compute. Each agent key must harbor a large, randomly seeded memory state for the whole epoch and use it to solve a memory-hard puzzle. The solution is a lantern that proves the state was really held. A sybil must allocate the same memory per identity, so k fake keys cost k times the RAM and bandwidth, and one machine cannot mint them cheaply. The state is a wide meadow of random data, expensive to store and hard to share without correlated timing. Honest agents pay once. Attackers pay per voice.
